sourcedFrom:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL FOR:
Colt® Anaconda™ Revolver — Rev. - (2020)
cleanIntro: A six-shot .44 Magnum double action that strips no further than an open cylinder. Colt's Anaconda procedure is a thirteen-step clean done against the swung-out cylinder, and the book then states the revolver is not to be field stripped — so there is no Deep Clean path in it.

steps.title: Read the barrel before anything else
steps.action: Find the cartridge designation stamped on the barrel and confirm it reads .44 Magnum. Colt's book for the Anaconda covers a six-shot, single/double action revolver in .44 Remington Magnum, in a 6-inch and an 8-inch version, with a shrouded ejector rod.
steps.prose: The two barrel lengths share one procedure; nothing in the cleaning changes between them. Sights are the part that varies: the standard front sight is a red ramp held by a #4-40 set screw, with Tritium, brass bead and fiber optic options, and Colt warns that the sights on your gun may differ from the ones it describes. If your Anaconda wears an optic or another accessory, its instructions come from that accessory's maker.
steps.quote: The cartridge designation is located on the barrel of the revolver (Figure 1). This indicates the correct ammunition that must be used in the revolver.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL FOR:
Colt® Anaconda™ Revolver — Rev. - — Characteristics of Revolver — Ammunition, p.7

steps.title: Hammer down, finger out, cylinder out to the left
steps.action: Keep your finger off the trigger and outside the guard, make sure the hammer is not cocked, then pull the cylinder latch rearward and push the cylinder out to the LEFT side of the frame.
steps.prose: Colt's latch is pulled back, not pushed forward or pressed in. If the cylinder will not swing out, look at the hammer rather than pushing harder: the hand blocks the cylinder from opening or closing whenever the hammer is cocked, and the big Anaconda cylinder gives you plenty of leverage to do damage with.
steps.quote: Open revolver by pulling cylinder latch to the rear and pushing the cylinder out to the left of the revolver.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL FOR:
Colt® Anaconda™ Revolver — Rev. - — Cleaning & Lubrication, step 3, p.17
steps.warn: Never force the cylinder open with the hammer cocked. Colt states this could damage the revolver mechanism.

steps.title: Eject, then look and feel all six
steps.action: Muzzle up, push the ejector rod rearward to force every live round or empty case out of the six chambers, take them off the gun, and let the rod return under its own spring. Then check every chamber by eye and by finger.
steps.prose: Fired .44 Magnum cases can grip their chambers, so push the rod fully and squarely rather than striking it. The rod should re-seat on its own; if it hangs partway, that is usually fouling behind the ratchet, and the cleaning screen for that area is the fix.
steps.quote: Push ejector rod rearward forcing out all live rounds or empty cartridge cases from the chambers. When they are clear of the chambers, remove from revolver.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL FOR:
Colt® Anaconda™ Revolver — Rev. - — Cleaning & Lubrication, step 4, p.17
steps.warn: Colt's own standard: the revolver is clear only when all chambers are empty and the hammer is in the uncocked position.

steps.title: Salt air, water, mud or sand — stop here
steps.action: If this Anaconda has been used in salt air or has been in water, mud or sand, do not bench-clean it. Colt's instruction is that it is completely disassembled, cleaned and inspected by a competent gunsmith or returned to Colt for service.
steps.prose: A big-bore hunting revolver is exactly the gun that ends up in the rain or dropped in a creek bed. Water and grit get behind the sideplate into the lockwork, where nothing done through an open cylinder can reach them.
steps.quote: Note: If the revolver has been used in salt air, water, mud, or sand, it should be completely disassembled, cleaned, and inspected by a competent gunsmith or returned to Colt for service.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL FOR:
Colt® Anaconda™ Revolver — Rev. - — Maintenance, p.15

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Cylinder out to the left, all six chambers empty, ejector rod seated. That is the whole strip Colt publishes for the Anaconda — the sideplate, the crane and the grips all stay on the gun.
steps.prose: Everything the cleaning procedure needs is now in reach: bore, six chambers, front face of the cylinder, rear face of the barrel, the frame, and the ratchet with the ejector rod pushed back. Colt says that going further than the book describes voids the service agreement, and that anything more goes to a competent gunsmith or back to Colt.
steps.quote: IMPORTANT: DO NOT FIELD STRIP YOUR REVOLVER. IF YOU DO SO YOU WILL VOID YOUR SERVICE AGREEMENT.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL FOR:
Colt® Anaconda™ Revolver — Rev. - — Cleaning & Lubrication, closing note, p.18

deepAbsentReason: Colt's Anaconda manual documents a cylinder-open clean only — thirteen numbered cleaning and lubrication steps on pp.17–18 covering the bore, the six chambers, the cylinder faces, the ratchet and the frame — and then states that the revolver is not to be field stripped, that doing so voids the service agreement, and that additional maintenance goes to a competent gunsmith or back to Colt (p.18; the same limit is printed in Maintenance, p.15). It publishes nothing further, so there is no deeper procedure to walk.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBERS
tasks: Clean the bore — bore brush or cleaning patch, according to how much has been fired since the last clean
Clean each of the six chambers the same way, with a chamber brush or a cleaning patch
Finish with a lightly oiled bore patch through the barrel and through every chamber, leaving a thin film

cleaning.name: CYLINDER FACES, RATCHET & FRAME
tasks: Small brush and a little cleaning solution on the front face of the cylinder, the rear face of the barrel and the frame
Clean the rear face of the cylinder and the ratchet, then push the ejector rod rearward and clean behind the ratchet
Wipe all cleaning solution off the revolver before any oil goes on

cleaning.name: OIL & WIPE DOWN
tasks: If the internals need it, cock the hammer and apply a few drops of oil to the internal components — Colt's 'if necessary', not a routine step
Wipe every external surface with a cloth lightly moistened with gun oil
Before firing, pass a dry bore patch through the barrel and each chamber to take out as much oil as possible
If your Anaconda carries a decorative finish, keep solvents, paint thinners and gun-cleaning products off it — Colt specifies a clean, soft cloth dampened with water for that surface

reassembly: Hammer down, push the cylinder into the frame until the cylinder latch moves forward into its closed position — never swing or slam it in.
Rotate the closed cylinder until the bolt engages it and it will not turn, so you know it is locked and indexed.
Dry-patch the bore and every chamber before firing.
fncheck: With every chamber confirmed empty and the hammer down: the cylinder latch should return fully forward and the cylinder should stay shut until the latch is pulled rearward; turning the closed cylinder clockwise by hand should end with the bolt engaged and the cylinder refusing to rotate; the cylinder should not open or close with the hammer cocked; and at rest there should be a gap between hammer and firing pin, because the transfer bar rises only while the trigger is held back. Anything that does not function properly goes to a competent gunsmith or back to Colt.
